items.label: section_header
items.text: DISPLACEMENT REACTIONS

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 19.3 In an exothermic reaction, chemical energy is converted to heat energy. Heat is released so the temperature goes up.

items.label: text
items.text: You will come across lots of exothermic reactions in this course. Some examples are given below.

items.label: text
items.text: Any reaction that produces a flame is exothermic. Burning things produces heat energy.

items.label: text
items.text: For instance, hydrogen burns in oxygen, producing water and lots of heat:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 H _ { 2 } ( g ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 H _ { 2 } O ( | )

items.label: text
items.text: Apart from burning, other exothermic changes include:

items.label: list_item
items.text: the reactions of metals with acids

items.label: list_item
items.text: neutralisation reactions

items.label: list_item
items.text: displacement reactions.

items.label: text
items.text: When magnesium reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, for example, the mixture gets very warm:

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow M g S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: About the only interesting thing that you can observe happening when sodium hydroxide solution reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid is that the temperature rises:

items.label: formula
items.text: N a O H ( a q ) + H C l ( a q ) \rightarrow N a C l ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } O ( 1 )
